title: OnsiteGene 4 Protocol for Saliva Sample Collection
author: yliu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bpjemkje
materials: Ensure all collection materials are labelled with the correct identifying information.
The total volume measured should exclude any bubbles.

steps.title: Prepare for Sample Collection
steps.instruction: Prepare the environment and the donor for saliva collection.

substeps.instruction: Clean hands using alcohol-based sanitizer or soap and water (no fragrances).
Wear appropriate PPE, including at minimum gloves and a mask.
Maintain maximum distance from the sample donor throughout the process.
Ensure the donor has avoided water for 10 minutes and other drinks, food, and nasal sprays for 30 minutes prior to collection.
Direct the sample donor to begin pooling saliva in their mouth (no coughing or sniffing required).

steps.title: Collect Saliva Sample
steps.instruction: Collect the saliva sample into the provided tube.

substeps.instruction: Open the lid of the saliva collection tube.
Direct the sample provider to gently expel saliva into the container until at least 500 μL is collected.
Securely replace the lid of the collection tube.

steps.title: Stabilize and Secure Sample
steps.instruction: Add storage media and prepare the tube for transport.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 μL of OnsiteGene storage media to each sample tube and secure the lid.
Sterilize the tube surface with 70% ethanol or a disinfecting wipe.
Place the sample in a secondary container or an appropriately labeled biohazard bag.
Dispose of gloves and register sample collection information, including date and time.

steps.title: Sample Transport and Mixing
steps.instruction: Transport the sample and mix the contents.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the sample at room temperature (virus RNA remains stable at room temperature for 3-5 days).
Vortex each sample collection tube for 5 seconds at 3000-5000 RPM, or alternatively, tap or shake the tube to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Extract RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample and perform automated RNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Spin down the tube for 15 seconds using a centrifuge to remove liquid from the cap and sediment solid particles.
Transfer 900 µL of supernatant into the cartridge of the OnsiteGene magnetic beads RNA extraction instrument.
Load the cartridge into the extraction instrument (processes up to 32 samples per run).
Run the extraction process for 6 minutes (no hands-on work) to obtain a 50 µL sample elution volume.

steps.title: Prepare RT-qPCR Reaction
steps.instruction: Set up the reaction tubes for amplification.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 7.5 µL of extracted RNA sample (which can be stored at -20°C for 14 days) and 7.5 µL of OnsiteGene Hi-Sense TM COVID-19 detection kit reaction mix (containing primers and probes) into a superfast RT-qPCR reaction tube.
Secure the lid of the tube.
Spin down the tube for 15 seconds using a centrifuge or spinner, or alternatively, shake the tube by hand to move samples to the bottom.

steps.title: Run RT-qPCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Load samples into the OnsiteGene XDive Superfast Real-Time PCT instrument and run the thermal cycling program.

substeps.instruction: Load up to 16 reaction tubes into the instrument.
Execute the following conditions: Step 1: 50°C for 30 sec; Step 2: 95°C for 0 sec; Step 3: 60°C for 2 sec; Step 4: Read Fluorescence intensity and overhead (10 sec).
Repeat steps 2-4 for 40 cycles.

steps.title: Interpret Results
steps.instruction: Report results based on the CT values of the Internal Control (IC) and SARS-CoV-2 targets (ORF1ab and N1).

substeps.instruction: Negative: IC CT ≤ 40 and both SARS-CoV-2 targets CT > 40.
Positive: IC CT ≤ 40 and any SARS-CoV-2 target CT ≤ 40.
Invalid: IC CT > 35 and both SARS-CoV-2 targets CT > 40 (indicates IC failure or insufficient specimen volume; retest sample).
